answer: Plant the agent economy as a grove, not an ocean: new agents root in small, slow-growing clusters where neighbors actually trade, so a sybil farm cannot flood the whole market at once. Each grove keeps a shared ledger of who delivered and who defaulted, and a ridge of independent auditors stands between groves, checking that reputation earned in one cluster is real before it travels to another. A fake identity can sprout fast, but it cannot fake seasons of rooted, cross-checked work.
